reviewedScope: On the delivered 614 bindless array-delta Core: DMA copies of R16G16B16A16Float and R32G32B32A32Float textures use the GPU-side copy for Hogwarts Legacy only (GraphicsConfig.HogwartsFloatDmaGpuCopy, set per session by the Library from the launched title; every other title keeps the MeloNX exclusion), into a block-linear destination with the same element size and a target sized in bytes; a destination texture that cannot be created falls back to the copy through guest memory (all formats). Every 2D copy still read through guest memory is attributed by bounded logging (each signature once, at most 8 per reason; counts per reason every 1024 copies, at most 64 times; no allocation per copy once full). For Hogwarts Legacy only (GraphicsConfig.HogwartsDmaRegionUpload, set with the float policy), a 2D copy from linear memory into a block-linear destination with identity components and one element size, whose destination surface is a single-level 2D uncompressed colour texture of the cache (the lookup of the direct upload of complete copies, at each width the GOB-aligned surface holds; ambiguous: none) at scale 1 without host format conversion, and whose region falls on whole texels inside it, without overlaps of an incompatible layout, is uploaded into that host texture region (rows packed as the host reads them) after the texture's memory synchronisation; guest memory is then patched as before but written untracked, so the texture and guest memory hold the same region, the texture is neither read back nor uploaded again, and its modified state is left as it was. Uploads, declines and guest-memory accesses over 2 ms are counted in the bounded summary (at most 64 lines). For Hogwarts Legacy only (the same policy), a 2D copy from linear memory whose source a GPU-modified linear texture alone holds (TextureGroup.AnyHandleModified; the copy's stride, single-level 2D uncompressed colour at scale 1, the whole source in one physical region, no other texture group over it, no incompatible overlap, the rectangle on whole texels inside the stride) into the texture of the destination surface with the same UNORM format unconverted by the host (another group, no incompatible overlap); under the policy the guest path reads its destination tracked unless the region was uploaded, is copied on the GPU (host region copy queued after the GPU writes, destination marked modified, as the upstream GPU copy of block-linear sources does) instead of reading the source through guest memory, which runs the source texture's flush action; TextureCache.FindOverlapsInRange (under the texture read lock) finds the source. Every slow source read is attributed to the overlapping textures (kind counted; each new signature logged once, at most 8). Build 621: for Hogwarts Legacy only, a 2D copy whose source is a block-linear surface that a GPU-modified texture of the cache is (the region-upload lookup; single-level 2D uncompressed colour at scale 1, no incompatible overlap, the rectangle on whole texels) is copied on the GPU (TryCopyGpuRegion) into the texture of a block-linear destination surface, found, or created over that surface as the delivered GPU copy of complete copies creates its target only when no texture of the cache overlaps the surface; same format, unconverted by the host, another group; both synchronised, the region copied by the host, the destination marked modified. The region lookup takes only a texture that starts at the surface base. Build 623: a read-back (a block-linear source region into linear memory) is deferred: copied on the GPU (TryReadBackGpuRegion) into a linear texture over the destination, found with the same layout and format or created when no texture overlaps it, without writing guest memory; a strict host sync is forced after the copy and a CPU read flushes the texture after it. Only whole contiguous rows on 4 bytes with no buffer of the cache over the destination (BufferCache.HasBufferInRange, a read-only query) qualify. The DMA summary counts read-back candidates, deferred ones, declines by reason and the first-access flushes of read-back textures (TextureGroup.ReadBackTarget: number, total and longest duration, GPU-thread ones). A byte model checks immediate, next-frame, partial and rewrite-before-read accesses against the reference copy with the real LayoutConverter. ThreadedRenderer times each command it runs by type and logs, every 5 s of rendering, the 8 command types with the most time (calls and milliseconds) to the core log. The Vulkan backend times on the render thread, for every title, each draw preparation (RenderStageTimer: the whole of RecreateGraphicsPipelineIfNeeded, now PrepareGraphicsDraw behind a timed wrapper, with its pipeline creation or lookup, barrier flush, descriptor update and auto-flush parts), each render pass begun (and those begun again on the framebuffer the last one ended on), each buffer fence wait (BufferHolder: before a direct write or for a read, on the render thread apart from other threads), each command buffer submission (FlushCommandsImpl, now SubmitCommands behind a timed wrapper, with its ReturnAndRent part) and each presentation (whole, image acquisition, queue present; Window.Present has no early return), and logs them every 5 s of presentation to the core log, then counts again; nothing else in these paths changes. Build 625: a read-back whose destination a buffer of the cache holds (build 624: 747 of 751, a whole 1x1 R16G16B16A16Float texture about once per frame) is copied on the GPU into that buffer when it covers the whole source texture and no texture overlaps the destination (BufferCache.TryCopyTextureToBuffer: ITexture.CopyTo of the level into the buffer range, the range marked GPU-modified as a buffer to buffer copy does), followed by a forced host sync; a partial region keeps the guest path and is counted. Build 626: when the only texture over that destination is the linear read-back target the first copies created (TextureGroup.ReadBackTarget, same layout and format), the copy goes into the buffer and into that texture, so both hold the latest bytes (build 625: 0 read-backs into buffers, 286 and 292 declined as occupied). Build 628: textures over that destination no longer decline the copy into the buffer; they get a write signal without a write, buffers exempt (PhysicalMemory.SignalTextureWrite), as a guest write there would give them; a buffer texture is left alone and a texture of the source group still declines (build 626: 0 read-backs into buffers, 352 and 742 declined as occupied). The first textures there are logged. Build 628, MoltenVK on a tile-based GPU (Hogwarts Legacy only, MoltenVkPolicy): the write-to-read barrier of a texture bound inside a render pass it is not an attachment of is deferred to the next begin of that pass (its forced fence), because MoltenVK restarts the Metal render pass for every GENERAL-layout image barrier recorded inside one and Metal's hazard tracking already orders the read after the attachment use of an ended pass (PipelineBase.TryDeferInPassReadBarrier, TextureStorage.QueueWriteToReadBarrier). A detail line gives the commands that ended the passes begun again, those barriers, the compute descriptor updates by program size, the first-chance exceptions and the GPU busy time from the Metal command buffers (MetalGpuTimer: -[MTLCommandBuffer commit] of the class of MoltenVK's queue replaced through the Objective-C runtime, the original always called). RenderStageTimer also times each compute dispatch preparation (pipelines, barriers, descriptors) and counts the render passes dispatches end. MoltenVK performance tracking is on (MVKConfiguration.PerformanceTracking, statistics logged every 300 presented frames to stderr). The DMA fixture runs the real RenderStageTimer with a logger double, and the fragmented-read fixture compiles the Vulkan backend from the final source. Both GPU copies take UNORM, sRGB and float formats (exact at their own size). Under the policy the guest path signals its source read and tracked destination read precisely (PhysicalMemory.SignalPreciseRead), and texture handles ignore a precise read outside their own bytes. For every title on Apple platforms, ThreadedRenderer raises the render and GPU threads, and the demand pipeline compile thread raises itself, to user-interactive QoS (a failed call logged once); the pipeline cache budget is 1 GiB (main 768 MiB, workers 128 MiB). Bindless delta passes skip the verification scan when no texture was invalidated during the pass (Texture.InvalidationEpoch) and visit only the pool ids logged since their last pass when that set is exact (TexturePool change log); otherwise the full scan or rebuild as before. The array-delta, fragmented-read (complete final GPU assembly), binding-snapshot and collector fixtures and the new DMA fixture rerun on the final source. Payload, SDK, ABI, source pin, smoke and all other lots unchanged; no physical gameplay, device allocation or FPS claim. Build 631, descriptor encoding (Hogwarts Legacy only, EncodingPolicy, assigned per session by the Library with the other policies; off, both paths are the delivered ones): the template path of DescriptorSetUpdater.UpdateAndBind indexes its scratch arrays by binding number, and they had one stage of elements (32 textures, 16 images), so a fragment texture (binding 64-95), a buffer texture or a buffer image threw IndexOutOfRangeException, caught by UpdateAndBindDescriptorSets, which then wrote the set again one descriptor at a time (build 629: 326 439 first-chance exceptions in 1067 frames); the scratch arrays are now sized like the references (MaxTextureBindings * 2, MaxImageBindings * 2) and, under the policy, the template path uses them whole (off: the one-stage lengths, as delivered); each template fallback is counted by set. A texture array (not a buffer array) records every element update by range (a log of 1024 ranges, the oldest half dropped past it), keeps descriptor sets of its own (at most 8, from the program's manual-set cache, released when the array is disposed) and brings an idle one (bound in no pending command buffer: PipelineLayoutCacheEntry.IsManualDescriptorSetCollectionIdle) up to date by writing only the elements changed since it was last written (whole when the log no longer holds them or more than a quarter changed); its element values are resolved from the changed ranges, and each command buffer references the distinct views and samplers once (counted incrementally for updates of up to 4096 elements, counted again otherwise), a destroyed one found there recorded as a change of its elements, which take the dummy. A binding that is not one array of the array's length, or every set pending, takes the delivered path (counted). Build 629: the 524 288-element bindless arrays were rewritten whole after each delta update of about 40 elements (7.7 ms per update, 30.7 ms of compute descriptor time per frame in heavy play). The detail line gives the template fallbacks by set and the array writes (whole, by range, elements kept, reference passes, current binds, sets added, delivered path). The scalar-texture, fallback-scratch, single-resource-binding and bounded-binding-snapshot fixtures, whose receipts declare DescriptorSetUpdater.cs or TextureArray.cs, rerun on the final source against the delivered one with the policy off and on; the last two run both TextureArrays compiled whole with the caller arrays overwritten as soon as a call returns. Build 631, occlusion reports (Hogwarts Legacy only, GpuContext.QueueSyncpointsBehindReports, assigned per session by the Library with the other policies; off, the delivered path): a syncpoint increment with pending reports, or behind queued ones, submits as before (CreateHostSyncIfNeeded StrictSyncpoint, Force when reports are pending), takes the pending reports (CounterCache.TakePendingReports) and joins a FIFO of the context instead of draining the threaded renderer and waiting for them; the GPU thread publishes each entry's reports and increments in order once they are complete (DeferredCounterReport.IsReady; GPFifoDevice.WaitForCommands, waits of 1 ms while the FIFO is not empty), drains the FIFO with the blocking flush (the renderer first runs the queued submissions, once per drain, as the blocking path) before a Syncpointb wait, before a 3D engine increment (ThreedClass.IncrementSyncpoint, counted apart) and when its head is 50 ms old; an entry leaves the FIFO once published, so a report that cannot complete withholds its increment at the head as the blocking path withholds it, and disposal increments what is left without publishing. Compiled fixture: order, waits, age, 3D increments, barrier, disposal, concurrent consumer (test/melonx_queued_syncpoints_fixture_test.py). Counted and logged every 4096 queued increments and at disposal. Build 629: 751 report flushes, 11.8 s of query read-backs in 90 s on the GPU thread. Core 639 adds the reviewed MeloNX FPS/stability lot of PR #153: the pipeline warm-up key carries the draw's alpha-to-coverage and alpha-to-one state (shader disk cache format unchanged) and names the fields of a remaining miss; while only the device is short and this process keeps a comfortable headroom, the texture trim evicts only textures it frees without a flush. Core 642 adds the reviewed MeloNX lot of PR #154: under MoltenVK 1.4.2 or later (MVK_VERSION above 10400, whose Metal hazard tracking no longer orders argument-buffer reads after an ended pass) the Hogwarts in-pass read barrier is recorded instead of deferred and the TBDR barrier batch keeps its ordering (MoltenVK 1.4.0 keeps the delivered deferral, one log line names the rule); the binding-sized template descriptor scratch of build 631 is used whole for every title (each other per-title policy keeps Hogwarts only); the DMA summary attributes read-backs declined as occupied to the textures there; a remaining background pipeline miss names the program and stage context. No physical gameplay or FPS claim. The build 87 barrier compaction proof declares BarrierBatch.cs, so it is rerun on the final source (barrier-compaction: the delivered class as control, every trace equal with MoltenVK 1.4.0 or another driver; with MoltenVK 1.4.1 or later the candidate ends the pass exactly where an in-pass image barrier of a tile-based GPU is for a non-attachment). Core 644 adds the reviewed MeloNX lot of PR #156: under the Hogwarts policy, a DMA read-back into a buffer no longer sends the textures over its destination a guest write signal without data (they reloaded zeros or an older value from untracked guest memory); each such texture that holds the destination's bytes at the source's texel places receives the source on the GPU (SynchronizeMemory, CopyTo, SignalModified), and any other overlap declines to the delivered guest path ("unreceivable"); the Gpu Window attributes each presented image (GPU-modified or reloaded, re-created, repeated address), bounded, diagnostics only. No physical gameplay, FPS or visual claim. Core 647 adds the PR #156 follow-up: VulkanRenderer.Dispose cancels every compile no worker has taken and joins the running ones before the per-program waits (the single background worker compiled the whole queue first: SSBU early closes of 15-30 s), a cancelled compile is no longer logged as a failure, and a durable gpuTeardown line attributes the close; at the first three host pauses the HLE records every application thread's state, wait kind and time since it last ran (diagnostics only). No physical gameplay claim. Core 649 adds the teardown phase marks: durable Core lines around the guest stop, the GPU release, the device idle wait and the swapchain release, so a close that never ends (SSBU while the screen is recorded) names its phase; journal only. Core 654 adds the PR #156 new lot from the IPA 650 device logs: SurfaceFlinger.Dispose unregisters each remaining layer's producer binder from the static HOSBinderDriverServer registry, which otherwise kept every closed session's Switch (producer, BufferQueueCore, KEvent, KernelContext) reachable for the rest of the process (342 and 690 MB of managed heap live after the two Hogwarts teardowns), and the Library records one durable sessionRetention line after the final collection (weak references only); the collector writes one durable gcEvent line per newly completed blocking or background gen2 collection (16 per kind per session, the final sample unbounded); RenderDetail counts the three suspected black-artifact paths every window (texture-array elements given the dummy view, MoltenVK attachment-only in-pass barriers kept inside the pass, write-mask-filtered attachments). Journal and counters apart from the binder release; no device run, no FPS or visual claim. MeloNX levers from the IPA 650 logs: the whole rebuilds of pool-sized bindless texture, sampler and image arrays (longer than 4096 elements) rent their arrays from bounded slots (TextureBindingsArrayCache: two per element type; GAL ThreadedArrayPool: eight per element type, under its lock; at most 1048576 elements per type), cleared on return, instead of allocating four large-object-heap arrays per threaded rebuild; the arrays given to the backend have the same lengths and contents. On iOS, when the device exposes VK_GOOGLE_display_timing, the Vulkan window paces a guest presenting at a steady multiple of its 60 Hz period on a lattice of display refreshes anchored on MoltenVK's presentedTime (desiredPresentTime; only at VSync Switch, as set by the Library; standing down when targets are not honoured), with one "Present pacing over" line per 5 s window. No device run, no FPS or smoothness claim. Core 658 (IPA 657 fix, MoltenVK v1.4.2 kept): MoltenVK 1.4.2 on iOS 18 and later relies on its MTLResidencySet for every argument-buffer descriptor and never adds the CAMetalLayer drawable to it, so the Vulkan window no longer writes the drawable with the PresentCopy compute shader (a storage image through a descriptor, which may not land: black launch, frozen or older frames); it draws the game image into the drawable with HelperShader.BlitColor (a render pass, the drawable as a color attachment, same regions and filter, alpha 1), and a FSR or Area scaling filter writes an RGBA8 texture of Ryujinx's before BlitColor copies it into the drawable; MetalFX and the clear unchanged; one Present path line per window. No device run, no visual claim. Core 661 (Hogwarts 658 logs, two players; maintainer request of 5 Nov: in-play RAM, GC pauses, left stick, then sky artifacts): the GPU thread polls a published program link status instead of draining the render queue; warm-up keys match geometry-as-compute and primitive-restart draws; SetProgram no longer waits for play-time warm-ups and a draw waits only for its own pipeline, cache persistence off that wait (Hogwarts policy); teardown cancels the compile backlog before program disposal and saves the main pipeline cache first; the forced {Nv} syncpoint wait goes on while the GPU progresses, with a no-progress guard and a hard cap (Hogwarts policy); the present pacer engages on the iPhone (stand-down fix, calibrated margins, learned offset); a closed session releases its statistics timer and time-service roots; journal-only gcEvent fallback flag, memory inventory and guest fault context; the LOH is compacted once after the first frame and in a held pause at device <= 15 %, never in play; a host memoryWarning at device <= 12 % runs the flush-free trim; cold pool-only sampler textures are released at device <= 10 % (bounded, reload pinning); pool texture arrays keep no all-null sampler arrays and one view per element; under MoltenVK 1.4.1+ residency-set ordering a texture read in a new stage after a write gets its own barrier, and Hogwarts render/compute switches without one get a full barrier; the NativeAOT workstation GC is the 10.0.0 library rebuilt with dotnet/runtime#119383 (run 41988362179), the build failing closed otherwise.; a Hogwarts read-back whose linear destination has no buffer but textures over one contiguous range goes into a buffer created there on the GPU (TryReadBackIntoBuffer: receivers fed, buffer textures left alone, what it cannot keep coherent keeps the guest path) instead of a texture flush per frame; with async shaders a draw whose program compiles is skipped only into a target the frame regenerates (every attachment drawn in the previous frame, one cleared whole in this one) or the presented image, and waits for its pipeline into any other target.; a texture flush references the image before recording its copy and records nothing for a destroyed one (no null image handle reaches vkCmdCopyImageToBuffer), the GPU texture flush then leaving guest memory unchanged; a pipeline creation error names its program once and the dropped draws are counted apart from async skips; a background pipeline compile first tries the main cache without waiting and without compiling (fail on compile required), then its worker cache.; a compute/graphics switch re-sends the resolved texture and image bindings instead of resolving every bound texture again (pool changes, channel switches and every other caller keep the full rebind); the session keeps the background GC thread alive with a non-blocking background gen2 request 12-16 s after the previous background gen2 for a managed heap of 384 MiB or more, so a later gen2 does not fall back to a blocking one. No device run, no FPS, memory or visual claim.
